newsitem.title: CANADA: Talisman no stranger to acquisitions.
newsitem.headline: Talisman no stranger to acquisitions.

text.p: Talisman Energy Inc, which late Wednesday revealed intentions to make a C$1.7 billion takeover bid for Wascana Energy Inc, has said often that acquisitions were a key part of its growth strategy.

In an much-anticipated announcement, Talisman of Calgary said it would offer C$18.50 ($13.69) cash or 0.41 of one of its shares for each share of Wascana, a former Saskatchewan government-owned oil company.

Since transforming itself into an independent Canadian energy firm from a branch plant of British Petroleum Co Plc at the start of the decade, Talisman, led by chief executive Jim Buckee, has become one of the country's largest independent oil and gas producers with operations worldwide.
Here is a list of Talisman's major acquisitions:
1992 - acquired Encor Ltd, a debt-hobbled Canadian firm that was once part of ill-fated Dome Petroleum, for C$514 million.

1994 - acquired Bow Valley Energy, a Canadian company with assets in western Canada, the North Sea and Indonesia, for C$1.8 billion. The move propelled Talisman into the international oil and gas arena.
1996 - acquired Britain's Goal Petroleum for C$333 million, adding to operations in the North Sea.
1996 - acquired interests in several North Sea fields for an undisclosed sum. The purchase included stakes in the Beatrice, Buchan and Clyde producing fields and Ross exploration block.
